name: Wolverine
first_appearance: Incredible Hulk #180–181 (Oct.–Nov. 1974); joined X-Men in Giant-Size X-Men #1 (May 1975)
bio: Feral, long-lived mutant with a healing factor and adamantium skeleton. Joined the X-Men as an outsider and became its heart. His friendships (Nightcrawler, Kitty, Storm) are among the warmest in the line; his rivalry with Cyclops is among the most bitter.

continuity.name: Earth-616
continuity.description: The main Marvel Comics continuity, running continuously since Fantastic Four #1 (1961).

era.name: Claremont Era
era.description: Giant-Size X-Men #1 (1975) through Chris Claremont's departure after X-Men #3 (1991). The all-new team, Phoenix, Days of Future Past, the Brood, Inferno.

relationships.label: Unrequited, mostly
relationships.summary: Logan's attraction to Jean is written as intense and almost never acted on; Jean's response varies by writer from fond refusal to genuine temptation. The relationship is largely about restraint, and it is consummated only in alternate futures.

events.note: Logan's interest in Jean is first made explicit.
Stranded on Asteroid M, Jean and Logan kiss; Logan kills her so the Phoenix will take over and save them.
Phoenix-Jean seeks out Logan; he refuses her repeatedly.

relationships.label: Teacher, then colleague
relationships.summary: Logan trained Kitty in Japan after her kidnapping by Ogun; she is the first of his series of young protégées (later Jubilee, Armor, Laura). As an adult she ran his school after his death.

events.note: Logan rescues and retrains Kitty in Japan; she takes the name Shadowcat.
Kitty is co-headmistress of the Jean Grey School.

relationships.label: Rivals for Jean, then for the X-Men
relationships.summary: Started as a love-triangle rivalry over Jean Grey and became a philosophical one: Logan, the soldier, came to believe children should be kept out of the war; Scott, the field leader, came to believe there was no one else to fight it. The 2011 Schism split the X-Men between them.

events.note: Logan joins; friction with Cyclops's leadership is immediate.
Wolverine's famous 'Now it's my turn' in the Hellfire Club, while Scott is captured.
The two fight on Utopia over whether to send students into battle; Wolverine leaves to reopen the school.
Logan sides with the Avengers against a Phoenix-possessed Cyclops.

relationships.label: Closest confidants, briefly lovers
relationships.summary: The two most senior members of the 1975 team, each the other's most trusted colleague. Written as a near-sibling friendship for decades, with a romantic period during Jason Aaron's Wolverine and the X-Men (2012–2014) that the line has mostly treated as a chapter rather than a change.

events.note: Storm takes over as team leader with Logan's backing.
Storm and Logan begin a relationship.
Logan dies; Storm leads the mourning.

relationships.label: Best friends; the devil and the saint
relationships.summary: The franchise's most consistently written male friendship. Kurt is the one person Logan does not perform for; Kurt's death in X-Force vol. 3 #26 (2010) broke Logan, and his return on Krakoa restored the pairing.

events.note: Early baseball-game issue establishing the team's off-duty bonds.
Nightcrawler dies saving Hope Summers; Logan carries the grief for years.
